evals.name: gate-waits-on-the-current-heads-run-not-the-pr-aggregate
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set, with the tracker answering as its § Tracker answers says: the branch is behind, the update moves the head from a1a1a1a to b2b2b2b, and the run for a1a1a1a is finished green while the run for b2b2b2b is in progress
evals.expected_output: The gate reads the head after the update, finds the run whose head is b2b2b2b, waits on that run, and only then reports the gate passed; the finished green run for a1a1a1a is named as the previous head's and never taken as the result.
assertions: the run waited on is the one whose head is b2b2b2b, the head after the update
the finished run for a1a1a1a is not taken as the gate's result
the response says why the head's run and not the PR's aggregate: a watch on the PR's checks reports the previous head's finished run
the gate is reported done only once the b2b2b2b run passes and the merge state reads clean

evals.name: behind-branch-is-updated-not-handed-back
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set, with the tracker answering as its § Tracker answers says: merge state BEHIND, no conflicts
evals.expected_output: The branch is brought up to date through the tracker's update-branch operation and the gate continues on the new head; nothing is handed back, and the report's last line says the branch was updated first.
assertions: the update-branch operation is performed rather than a hand back
the gate continues on the head the update produced
the report's last line says the branch was updated first
hand back is reserved for a red check or a conflicting update, neither of which the fixture presents

evals.name: middle-child-leaves-the-parent-open-and-counts-the-remaining
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set, with the tracker answering as its § Tracker answers and § Close answers say: PR #12 merges, #9 closes, and the parent #7 still has #11 open
evals.expected_output: #9 is closed with one comment naming PR #12, although the body's "Implements #9" is no closing keyword; the parent #7 is read from #9's Parent section, its children listed, #11 found open, and #7 left open with the report saying one child remains.
assertions: #9 is closed with a comment naming PR #12, and the body's wording is not relied on to close it
the parent is read from the ticket and its children are listed before any decision about it
#7 is left open because #11 is still open
the report states the parent's state as open with one child remaining

evals.name: last-child-closes-the-parent-with-every-childs-pr
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set § Variant — last child, with the tracker answering as that section says: merge state CLEAN, PR #14 merges, #11 closes, and every child of #7 then reads closed
evals.expected_output: #11 is closed with one comment naming PR #14; the parent #7 is read, its children #8, #9, #11 all found closed, and #7 is closed with one comment listing PRs #10, #12 and #14.
assertions: #11 is closed with a comment naming PR #14
#7 is closed only after every child is found closed
the closing comment on #7 lists all three PRs: #10, #12, #14
the report states the parent's state as closed with the PR list

evals.name: fired-trigger-is-acted-on-with-the-pr-named

evals.expected_output: The guidance file's § The public changelog is read as the post-merge section and its three triggers taken against PR #12's diff: the shelf-order trigger fires on src/shelves/finished/shelf.ts, the other two did not. The target is searched first and returns nothing, so an issue is opened in acme/site naming acme/reader#12 and what the page should now say. The report marks the first trigger fired-and-done with acme/site#31, and the other two did-not-fire.
assertions: the post-merge section is found by reading the guidance file, and each of its three triggers is taken against the diff
the shelf-order trigger is marked fired, and the shelf-added and shortcut triggers are marked did-not-fire
the target is searched for an open issue before one is opened
the issue opened names PR #12 and what the page should now say
the report names every trigger's state, fired ones with their issue

evals.name: no-post-merge-section-is-reported-and-costs-nothing-further
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set through the merge and close, then fixtures/guidance-without-triggers
evals.expected_output: The guidance file is read, no section stating what must happen when a change lands is found, and the step ends with the report saying "no post-merge section"; the diff is not taken against anything, no target is searched, and no issue is opened.

the report's trigger line reads no post-merge section
no issue is opened and no target is searched

evals.name: existing-open-issue-is-linked-not-duplicated
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set through the merge and close, then fixtures/guidance-with-triggers with the target answering as its § Target answers — Existing issue says: the search returns acme/site#29, open, naming acme/reader#10 and not #12
evals.expected_output: The shelf-order trigger fires; the search of acme/site finds #29 open for the same change, so no second issue is opened. #29 is linked in the report as fired-and-already-covered, and one comment is added there naming acme/reader#12 since the issue did not name it yet.
assertions: the target is searched before any issue is opened
acme/site#29 is recognised as covering the fired trigger and no new issue is created
a comment naming PR #12 is added to #29 because its body names only #10
the report marks the trigger fired-and-already-covered with #29 linked, and the other two did-not-fire

evals.name: frontier-names-the-ticket-this-merge-unblocked-in-the-five-line-shape
evals.fixture: fixtures/ticket-set through the merge and close, then fixtures/guidance-without-triggers, with the tracker answering as ticket-set's § Frontier answers says: #11 is the family's one open ticket, and its only blocked-by edge is #9, closed
evals.expected_output: The family's open tickets are listed and #11's blocking edges read through the tracker's native dependencies; #11 has no open blocker, so it is the frontier, and since #9 — the ticket just closed — is among its blockers, #11 is named as what this merge unblocked. The report is five lines in order: the merge commit, #9 closed with #7 open and one child remaining, no post-merge section, the frontier #11 with #11 newly unblocked, and that the branch was updated first.
assertions: the frontier is computed from the blocked-by edges of the family's open tickets, read through native dependencies, and names #11
#11 is named separately as unblocked by this merge because #9 was its last open blocker
the report is five lines in the order merge, close, triggers, frontier, handed back
the frontier line carries both the frontier and what was unblocked, and the last line says the branch was updated first
